cues.text: So tell me about your research project, John
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: I created a questionnaire for the study to determine people’s opinions of the relative feasibility of earning a living in Brisbane.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Oh, cool. How is it scored? Are they all multiple choice questions?
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Well, the questions consist primarily of yes/no responses. There are two free response questions at the end. Participants will use a computer to fill in their answer; that way it is really easy to analyse the data afterward.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Great! It sounds like you have a pretty solid idea of what you should do. Just don't forget to submit a copy of your plans to Professor Curran by the 15th.
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Oh, I almost forgot!
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Hm, you don’t do it for high grade or praise, but he can review and give you feedback.
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Right, that will be helpful - he has been conducting studies like this for 30 years now.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Yep, oh and I’m curious - are you going to be in the room giving subjects directions for the questionnaire?
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Well, I think the instructions will be provided by another representative who will not be analysing the data. I want them to feel they can answer and be completely anonymous, so I will not be in the room. Anonymity is really important for this study.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: I agree. Good idea. You should tell the representative to remind subjects to fully consider both sides of each issue. Sometimes it’s really easy to immediately check “yes” or “no” without stopping to think about it completely.
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: That’s so true! It’s like a race to finish the questionnaire first or something. I’ll make sure to include that in the instructions. This report has to be perfect!
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Wow, what’s the big deal? I know it’s part of your grade and all…
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Well it’s that, but also a well-executed study could grab the attention of faculty in the department, which would be a huge deal.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: So… for attention?
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: No silly! I mean I could really gain the respect of professors who may later take me on as a graduate student in their labs.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Oh, I see.
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Let me take a look at the survey. Wow, this looks great! The map of the median income by region is a great tool - where did you find it?
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Well thanks! I read a lot of sources and just noticed this one in a small psychology journal called Modern Psychology. It’s more helpful than the photo I added, but I think the photo is just so interesting. It was in the newspaper last year during that huge wage strike.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: It’s great. Probably not necessary, but it looks great. I don’t understand - what is WKRX’s involvement here?
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Oh - the radio station agreed to sponsor the study if I play their station in the room.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Wow, interesting. So you don’t have to pay for any of this?
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Exactly.
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: Nice! Where did you get that idea?
cues.speaker: Dani

cues.text: Last month at the Psychology Club Council meeting someone talked about how easy it is to get sponsorship from local businesses, so I listened to their advice and called around!
cues.speaker: John

cues.text: I’ll have to remember that. Well, this all looks great. Good luck!
cues.speaker: Dani
